summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Fixed Deposit taxation in India, including interest taxation, TDS rules, and tax-saving FDs. However, some key TDS thresholds have been updated for the current financial year (FY 2025-26) which are not reflected in the article.

claims.claim: Interest earned on a Fixed Deposit is classified under the head 'Income from Other Sources' as per the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that FD interest is taxable as 'Income from Other Sources' under the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: Banks deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) if your FD interest exceeds ₹40,000 (₹50,000 for senior citizens) in a financial year.
claims.note: For FY 2025-26, the TDS threshold for individuals below 60 years is ₹50,000 and for senior citizens is ₹1,00,000. The article's figures were applicable for FY 2024-25.

claims.claim: If you have not provided your PAN, the TDS rate jumps to 20%.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that if PAN is not provided, the TDS rate on FD interest is 20%.

claims.claim: You can submit Form 15G (for non-senior citizens) or Form 15H (for senior citizens) to avoid TDS if your total income is below the taxable limit.
claims.note: Forms 15G and 15H are indeed used by eligible taxpayers (non-senior citizens and senior citizens, respectively) to avoid TDS if their total income is below the taxable limit.

claims.claim: Tax-Saving FDs come with a mandatory lock-in period of 5 years. The principal amount invested in these FDs, up to a maximum of ₹1.5 lakhs in a financial year, is eligible for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: Tax-saving FDs have a 5-year lock-in period and investments up to ₹1.5 lakh qualify for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: For cumulative FDs, the interest is taxable on an accrual basis each financial year, even if you don't physically receive it until maturity.
claims.note: Interest on cumulative FDs is indeed taxable on an accrual basis annually, even if received at maturity.

article_title: Fixed Deposits: Tax on FD Interest & Key Rules for Depositors
